findings.claim: Speed drift is at rounding on flat Cartesian charts, where every method is exact

hypothesis: Without renormalization the speed invariant g(v, v) drifts at the global order of each method, and a non-unit initial speed is carried unchanged, showing that nothing resets it.
input_data: Speed-1.3 starts on the sphere, torus and hyperbolic plane (RK4, midpoint and Euler with 128 steps, adaptive rtol 1e-10); y' = y growth probes
Renormalized Euler on the sphere path with [64, 128, 256, 512] steps
mathematical_model: g(v, v) is a first integral of the geodesic flow; for a p-th order method its global defect is O(h^p). A renormalizing step would force g(v, v) = 1 whatever the initial speed.
numerical_result: Drift orders: euler sphere 1.02, saddle 1, torus 1, gaussian-bump 1, hyperbolic-plane 1.01, plane-polar 0.978, cylinder-polar 1.01; midpoint sphere 1.98, saddle 2.01, torus 2, gaussian-bump 2, hyperbolic-plane 2.03, plane-polar 2.01, cylinder-polar 2.01; rk4 sphere 3.91, saddle 4.02, torus 4, gaussian-bump 3.96, hyperbolic-plane 4, plane-polar 3.96, cylinder-polar 4; speed-1.3 starts keep |g - 1.69| <= 2.14e-08 (RK4, adaptive); renormalized Euler endpoint error 0.0139 at N = 128 (order 1.01) with speed drift 4.44e-16.
observation_model: max over nodes of |g(v, v) - 1| (or |g - 1.69|) evaluated with the exact metric.
